do_more: Focus on concrete, quirky physical objects as psychological metaphors like mugs and raincoats.
Use active, high-stakes narrative scenarios in titles rather than abstract descriptive phrases.
Keep the emotional tone immediately relatable and slightly absurd from frame one.
avoid: Using computer science or digital metaphors like open browser tabs that feel dry.
Using generalized conceptual titles like 'Choice Overload' without a tangible anchor.
Starting with a slow definition instead of dropping Leo and Mia right into a funny dilemma.
title_style: Winning titles use the format 'The [Specific Everyday Object] [Unusual Noun]', creating immediate curiosity through quirky juxtaposition.
next_tests: Test an object-based paradox about procrastination using a ridiculously specific household item.
Test an episode featuring a social awkwardness psychology concept tied to a single piece of clothing or food.
Test starting the hook mid-argument between Leo and Mia over a minor illogical habit.
